Hidden Manna
HID-n MAN-uh
noun phrase
From Revelation 2:17, the reward promised to the overcomer at Pergamos: "To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna." It recalls the pot of manna laid up before the LORD in the ark (Exo 16:33-34).

📖 Biblical Definition

The hidden manna is the reward the glorified Christ promises to the overcomer at Pergamos: "To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written" (Rev 2:17). The image reaches back to the wilderness, where God fed Israel with manna, "bread from heaven," and commanded that a golden pot of it be laid up before the testimony in the ark as a memorial (Exo 16:32-34; Heb 9:4). That manna was hidden in the holiest place, unseen by the people. To the church at Pergamos — pressed to eat "things sacrificed unto idols" at the pagan feasts — Christ offers a better and secret food: Himself, the true bread from heaven (John 6:48-51). Those who refuse the idol's table are given to feed, hidden and unseen by the world, on the living Christ now, and to feast openly with Him in glory. The hidden manna is thus the soul's secret nourishment in communion with the Lord, the inner sustenance the world cannot see or share, kept for those who overcome the seductions of compromise. It is the answer of heaven to the believer who will not trade Christ for the brief satisfactions of idolatry.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The reward promised to the Pergamos overcomer in Revelation 2:17 — a secret, heavenly food recalling the manna laid up in the ark; Christ Himself, the true bread from heaven, the soul's hidden nourishment for those who refuse the idol's table.

📖 Key Scripture

Rev 2:17 — "He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it."

Exo 16:33 — "And Moses said unto Aaron, Take a pot, and put an omer full of manna therein, and lay it up before the LORD, to be kept for your generations."

John 6:51 — "I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world."

Psa 78:24 — "And had rained down manna upon them to eat, and had given them of the corn of heaven."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The hidden manna is corrupted when it is reduced to bare symbol with no living Christ to feed on, or when the secret communion it promises is replaced by a religion of mere outward experience and spectacle.

expand to see more

Christ-emptied symbolism. Treated as a poetic flourish, the hidden manna becomes a vague image of reward with no substance. Scripture fills it: the true bread from heaven is Christ Himself, given for the life of the world, on whom the soul feeds by faith (John 6). The dictionary holds that the promise is no empty figure but a pledge of real communion — the overcomer is nourished now and forever on the living Lord he refused to trade for idols.

Few entries face direct postmodern redefinition; here the danger is reductive. Where the hidden manna names a secret, inward feeding on Christ that the world cannot see, a spectacle-driven religion prizes only the visible and the sensational. The principle to recover is the hiddenness of true communion: the deepest nourishment of the saints is unseen by the world, kept in the holy place of fellowship with God, and tasted by those who overcome rather than by those who perform.
